Data engineering, AI & software consultancy · Ahmedabad, India

## Data engineering, AI and software consulting that works in your timezone.

MV.tech is a remote-first consultancy based in Ahmedabad, India. We help companies make reporting reliable, automate manual work and build business applications and AI systems. Work with us on a defined project or add senior specialists to your team, with direct access to the engineers and collaboration hours agreed in your timezone.

What we do

### Build a system, improve a workflow or strengthen your team.

01 / Offshore data team

#### Offshore data engineering team

Dedicated data engineering and analytics capacity from India for ETL, warehouses, BI, migration and data quality work, with overlap hours agreed around your timezone.

02 / Data

#### Data engineering consulting

ETL and ELT pipelines, BigQuery, Snowflake and Redshift warehouses, migrations off legacy reporting, semantic models and data quality checks. Python and SQL done properly.

03 / Software

#### Custom software development

Business web applications, client portals, dashboards and internal tools, with the interface, integrations and data backend designed together.

04 / AI

#### AI automation, RAG & MCP development

Knowledge assistants grounded in your documents, Model Context Protocol servers that expose approved tools, and LLM features integrated into existing products.

05 / Automation

#### Workflow automation & API integration

Connect the systems your team moves data between by hand. Scheduled jobs, webhooks, validation and monitoring with clear ownership.

06 / Team

#### IT staff augmentation

Add a senior remote data, software, cloud or AI consultant to your existing team, with capacity, responsibilities and overlap hours agreed up front.

07 / Hiring

#### Technology recruitment

Hire permanent AI, data, software and cloud professionals into your own organisation, with an engineer shaping the brief and assessing fit.

Data warehouse migrationBusiness intelligence & dashboardsMCP servers & AI connectorsBlockchain data analytics
How remote works with us

### Based in India. Working in your hours.

India Standard Time sits between the Asia-Pacific and American working days, which lets a team in Ahmedabad share a real working window with almost any client. Before an engagement starts we agree when we overlap, how decisions get recorded and how you see progress between calls.

- Agreed collaboration hours — A recurring window in your timezone for standups, reviews and releases. Share the hours your team needs; we confirm coverage and account for daylight-saving changes before starting.
- Written progress you can forward — Decisions, demos and open questions are documented in your tools, so your stakeholders stay informed without another meeting.
- The people you meet do the work — No account managers or hand-offs to a junior bench. Scope, estimates and delivery come from the same senior engineers.
Engagement models

### Choose the working model that fits the work.

#### Scoped project

A defined outcome with milestones, acceptance criteria and handover. Best for a first data pipeline, an application, an automation or an AI assistant with a clear boundary.

#### Embedded consultant or team

Senior specialists working inside your team, in your tools and your hours, for an agreed capacity and duration. Best when you need depth and pace without a permanent hire.

#### Permanent recruitment

Hire into your own organisation with an engineering-led search: a clear role brief, agreed screening and candidates for your team to assess. Best when the role is long-term.

Choose between a project, embedded capacity and a permanent hire
| Consideration | Scoped project | Staff augmentation | Technology recruitment |
| What you need | A defined system or improvement delivered | Specialist capacity within an existing team | A permanent employee in your organisation |
| Who directs the work | MV.tech owns the agreed delivery scope | Your leads direct the agreed consultant workstream | Your organisation selects and employs the candidate |
| What we agree first | First milestone, acceptance criteria and handover | Role, capacity, duration and overlap hours | Hiring brief, screening, search scope and fees |
| What to bring to the first call | Current systems and the outcome you need | Backlog, required skills and team setup | Responsibilities, compensation and hiring timeline |

Common questions

### What people ask before they book a call.

More detail is in the full FAQ and on how we work.

**What does MV.tech do?**
MV.tech is a remote-first consultancy that provides data engineering, custom software development, workflow automation, AI development (including RAG systems and MCP servers), IT staff augmentation and technology recruitment. We are based in Ahmedabad, India, and work with clients worldwide.

**Can MV.tech provide an offshore data engineering team?**
Yes. MV.tech provides offshore data engineering and analytics capacity from India for ETL, cloud warehouses, BI, reporting, workflow automation and AI systems. We agree the workstream, required skills, allocated capacity and overlap hours before starting. See our offshore data engineering service.

**How does timezone overlap work with a team in India?**
We agree a recurring collaboration window in your local time before the engagement begins, for example 9:00 am to 1:00 pm US Eastern, 9:00 am to 3:30 pm in the UK, or 12:30 pm to 6:00 pm in Sydney. Standups, reviews and releases happen inside that window; written updates and documented decisions cover the rest of the day.

**How much does an MV.tech engagement cost?**
Pricing depends on scope, complexity, delivery capacity and support. Projects are priced against agreed deliverables; embedded consultants are priced on capacity and duration; recruitment fees are agreed per role. Share the outcome, current systems and any budget range so we can propose a useful first scope and price it before you commit.

**How does an engagement start?**
Book a 30-minute call or email a short brief. We clarify the goal, current systems and constraints, then propose a first milestone with deliverables, review points and the overlap hours. Work starts only after that scope is agreed in writing.

**Can MV.tech work inside our existing team and tools?**
Yes. Through IT staff augmentation our consultants join your team in your repositories, ticketing and communication tools, under the direction of your technical leads, with agreed capacity and responsibilities. We can also own a scoped project end to end.

**How can I identify the official MV.tech company?**
Our official brand is MV.tech and our website is mvtech.solutions. We are the consultancy founded by Meet Vaghasia in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. If you find similarly named companies while searching for MV Tech or MVTech, check the domain, founder and official LinkedIn profile.

About MV.tech

## Data, software and AI specialists, led by an engineer.

MV.tech is a data engineering, software development and AI consultancy founded by Meet Vaghasia in 2022 and based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. We build cloud warehouses, reliable reporting, business applications and AI automation for companies worldwide. Our remote team works directly with your technical and business teams, with responsibilities and timezone overlap agreed before delivery starts.

Founder

### Meet the engineer behind MV.tech.

### Meet Vaghasia — Founder & Lead Engineer

Meet is a senior data and AI engineer. His hands-on work covers Python and SQL pipelines into BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift and PostgreSQL, enterprise analytics migrations off legacy databases and manual reporting, dimensional and semantic models behind Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio and Streamlit, and AI automation built with RAG, Model Context Protocol servers and custom AI connectors. He is Toptal-vetted (Top 3% of applicants) and holds Google Cloud and IBM credentials.

That experience runs from enterprise reporting estates and financial data platforms through to on-chain analytics, which is why MV.tech treats reconciliation, access control, documentation and handover as part of the build rather than a later phase. He founded the company to give clients direct access to senior engineering without the layers, bench costs and hand-offs of a large consultancy.

Pricing is agreed against a written scope, or the capacity and duration of an embedded role. Deliverables, testing, documentation and support expectations are clear before you commit.

Every engagement starts with a first milestone, acceptance criteria and review points. You can judge the working relationship on something real before expanding it.

#### Careful with your data

Least-privilege access, separated environments and credentials handled the way you would expect from an engineering team that also runs production systems. See our delivery standards.

#### Honest about fit

If a problem does not need us, or needs something other than software, we say so on the first call. Long relationships come from useful advice, not from selling every project.

# MV.tech Brand Kit: Logos, Colours, Fonts & Guidelines

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/brand/
Description: Download the MV.tech brand kit: vector logos, favicons, avatars, the colour palette as design tokens, Inter fonts, icons and the full brand guidelines.
Last modified: 2026-09-12

Brand assets

## The MV.tech brand kit, ready to use.

Everything you need to represent MV.tech correctly in an article, a partner deck, a directory listing or a co-branded page. Vector logo masters, favicons and avatars, the colour palette as design tokens, the Inter type family, the icon set and the full guidelines.

Download the brand kit ZIP · 15 MB Ask for print files

What is inside

### Eight folders, no guesswork.

#### Vector masters

The logo as true vector, SVG and PDF, in every variant: horizontal, primary and vertical lockups, the monogram and the wordmark, each in dark, light and single colour. Send these to printers and designers.

#### Ready-made exports

PNG at 512 and 1024 pixels for every variant, so you rarely need to open a vector editor.

#### Favicons and app icons

favicon.ico, an SVG favicon, Apple touch icon, Android and maskable icons, a Safari pinned-tab mark and a ready-made head snippet.

#### Social avatars

Circle-safe profile images sized for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp and Google Business.

#### Colour and design tokens

The palette as JSON, CSS custom properties, SCSS, a Tailwind config, W3C design tokens, Adobe and GIMP swatches, and an Office theme.

#### Type

Inter for desktop and web with its open font licence, plus a type specimen and the rules for sizes, weights and letter-spacing.

#### Icon set

Brand icons in three colourways as SVG and PNG, with app-style tiles.

#### Guidelines

The full brand guidelines and a one-page quick reference covering logo use, clear space, minimum sizes, colour, accessibility and misuse.

Using the logo

### Five rules that cover almost every case.

- Use the vector masters.They are the source of truth. The PNGs are for everyday work.
- Match the logo to the background.Dark surfaces take the silver logo, white and pale surfaces the navy one.
- When you cannot control the background,use a file ending-on-inkor-on-white. Each carries its own background and clear space.
- Keep one dot of clear space.Nothing may enter the area around the logo equal to the teal dot's diameter.
- MV never appears twice.The monogram is the letters M and V, and its dot is the full stop, so a lockup pairs the mark withtechonly, never with the full wordmark. Never retype the wordmark in a font.
Do not stretch, rotate, recolour or add effects to the logo, and do not place it on a busy or low-contrast area. The guidelines in the download show the misuses in full.

Colour

### The palette, and where each colour is allowed.

| Name | Hex | Use |
| Ink | #05060B | Primary dark background |
| Navy | #071118 | Body text on light backgrounds, and the mark on white |
| Signal Teal | #10F5D0 | Accent and highlights on dark. Decorative only on white |
| System Cyan | #00BFCB | Gradient support and separators |
| Teal Ink | #007E7B | The only teal for links and small text on white |
| Silver | #F4F6F8 | Light surfaces and the mark on dark |
| Graphite | #405466 | Secondary text on light backgrounds |
Signal Teal and System Cyan do not meet accessibility contrast requirements for text on white, so on light backgrounds they are used for shapes and borders rather than words. Full contrast data ships with the download.

### Need the print files?

The download covers logos, colour, type, icons and the guidelines. Print-ready business cards with bleed and crop marks, letterhead, the company one-pager, Word and PowerPoint templates, email signatures and the complete social set are part of the full kit. Ask us and we will send them.

# Privacy, Security & Delivery Standards | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/compliance/
Description: How MV.tech handles client data, credentials and access: secure remote delivery, accessibility, website analytics and responsible use of automation and AI.
Last modified: 2026-10-07

Trust, security & compliance

## Professional delivery standards for responsible systems.

Practical security, careful data handling, transparent communication and clear project boundaries. This page explains how we work with your data and systems, and how this website itself handles visitor information.

Delivery standards

### What you can expect on every engagement.

#### Data privacy

Client data is handled only for agreed project purposes, with access limited to what delivery needs. We work in your environments where possible and do not retain client data after handover unless a support agreement requires it.

#### Secure delivery

Least-privilege access granted by you, separated development and production environments, secrets kept in your secret management, API security and access reviews during the engagement and at handover.

#### Accessibility

Web interfaces are planned with semantic structure, keyboard navigation, readable contrast and responsive layouts, following WCAG 2.1 AA as the working target unless a project specifies otherwise.

#### Clear terms

Scope, ownership, timelines, support and third-party responsibilities are documented before work begins. Mutual NDAs and your master services agreement are welcome.

This website

### Privacy notice for visitors.

- Information you send us
  Details submitted by email or through our scheduling link are used to respond to your enquiry, prepare proposals, deliver agreed services and maintain client communication. We do not sell or share enquiry data with third parties for marketing.
- Analytics
  This site uses Google Analytics 4 to understand aggregate traffic and improve the website. Analytics measures clicks on contact links as "intent", not as confirmed enquiries. Google Analytics loads when a page loads and sets its cookies immediately; this site does not show a consent banner, so there is no prompt to accept or reject it. To opt out, block analytics cookies or the googletagmanager.com domain in your browser settings or an extension, use a browser that blocks trackers by default, or install Google'sAnalytics opt-out add-on.
- Scheduling
  Calls are booked through Calendly. When you use the embedded calendar or booking link, Calendly's own privacy policy applies to the information you enter there.
- No accounts or portals
  This website is public marketing content. It does not offer a login, client portal or SSO endpoint, and it does not host private client data.
- AI crawlers
  Public pages may be read by search engines and AI assistants so that people can find accurate information about MV.tech. Machine-readable summaries are published at/llms.txtand/llms-full.txt.
- Contact
  Questions about this notice or about your data:contact@mvtech.solutions.
Responsible use

### Automation, data extraction and AI, done properly.

- Authorised access only. Integrations and data extraction use supported interfaces, honour source terms and rate limits, and are limited to client-approved use cases.
- Humans stay in control. Automated workflows keep review where judgment is required; AI assistants act only on approved data and tools, with permissions enforced in the application rather than in a prompt.
- Evaluated before expansion. AI features are tested against real questions and failure cases, including what happens when the answer is not in the source material, before their audience is widened.
- Your data stays yours. Client data is not used to train third-party models, and any use of AI tooling in delivery follows your policies.
Security or compliance questions?

### Ask before we start. We prefer it.

Procurement, security and legal questions are easiest to answer at the scoping stage. Bring your requirements and we will tell you plainly what we can and cannot commit to.

What happens next

### From first call to a written next step.

- 01 — We talk for 30 minutes — You describe the result you need, the current setup and your constraints. We ask the questions an engineer would ask and tell you honestly whether we are the right fit.
- 02 — We define the next step in writing — When the requirement is clear, we propose a first milestone with deliverables, acceptance criteria, assumptions, overlap hours and a price. If technical questions remain, we explain the review or discovery needed to scope it.
- 03 — You agree the scope before work starts — We confirm responsibilities, availability and commercial terms, then set up access and begin delivering work you can review. A first enquiry does not commit you to an engagement.
Three things to bring

### Make the first conversation count.

- The result you need. The workflow, report, application or AI feature, and what should be better when the work is done.
- The current setup. The systems involved, what already works and what keeps getting in the way. A description or a sanitised example is enough to start.
- Your working constraints. Timezone, preferred overlap, target date and any budget range. These shape a useful first scope.

Who we work with

Whether you are validating a first product or modernising a large reporting estate, the engineering standards are the same: traceable data, controlled access, documentation and monitoring.

First data and product infrastructure built with scale in mind but without premature complexity: one warehouse, clear definitions, a dashboard people believe.

#### Enterprise data teams

Migrating legacy databases and manual reporting into Snowflake or BigQuery, rebuilding semantic and BI layers, and adding specialist capacity alongside internal teams.

# MV.tech FAQ: Services, Pricing, Timezones & How to Start

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/faq/
Description: Get to know MV.tech in Ahmedabad, India: data and AI services, project pricing, remote collaboration hours, security, hiring options and the first scoping call.
Last modified: 2026-10-07

FAQ

## Remote consulting questions, answered plainly.

Everything people usually want to know before booking a call: who we are, where we are, how timezones and costs work, what we build and how we protect your data. If your question is not here, ask us directly.

The company

### Who MV.tech is.

**What is MV.tech?**
MV.tech is a remote-first technology consultancy founded by Meet Vaghasia in 2022 and based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. We provide data engineering, business intelligence, custom software, workflow automation, AI development (including RAG systems and MCP servers), blockchain data analytics, IT staff augmentation and technology recruitment to clients worldwide. See our company facts and founder background.

**How do I identify MV.tech among similarly named companies?**
Our official brand is MV.tech, our website is mvtech.solutions and our founder is Meet Vaghasia in Ahmedabad, India. When searching for MV Tech, MVTech or MV Tech Solutions, check those details and our official LinkedIn profile. A similar company name alone does not establish a connection to MV.tech.

**Where is MV.tech based, and where are your clients?**
We are based in Ahmedabad, India, and deliver fully remotely. Our clients are in India and worldwide, including North America, the United Kingdom, continental Europe, the Gulf and Asia-Pacific.

**How big is the team?**
Deliberately small. MV.tech is a focused team of senior specialists across data, software, cloud, automation and AI, led by founder Meet Vaghasia. We scale a specific engagement with additional specialists when the scope needs it, and say so when it does not.

**What experience do MV.tech's engineers bring?**
Our engineers have worked with organisations including Google, Volvo, BCW, RootstockLabs, Chainlabs, Toptal and Turing, directly or through vetted talent platforms. These names describe team members' professional experience, not endorsements, current partnerships or a list of direct MV.tech clients. Review the expertise and credentials page and the founder's linked professional profiles, then ask about experience relevant to your workstream.

Timezones & cost

### Working with a team in India.

**Can a team in India overlap US, UK, European or Australian working hours?**
Yes. India Standard Time (UTC+5:30) overlaps the working day of every major business region for part of the day. Typical collaboration windows we plan around are 9:00 am to 1:00 pm US Eastern, 7:00 am to 10:00 am US Pacific, 9:00 am to 3:30 pm in the UK, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm in Central Europe, most of the business day in the Gulf, and 12:30 pm to 6:00 pm in eastern Australia. Exact hours are agreed per engagement.

**Does timezone overlap mean 24/7 support?**
No. Overlap means agreed working hours for collaboration: standups, reviews, demos and releases. Any support coverage, response-time expectations or release windows are defined separately in the engagement scope.

**How does MV.tech keep consulting costs lean?**
MV.tech operates as a focused remote team with direct access to the engineers doing the work. We scope an initial milestone so you can assess delivery before expanding it. The total cost still depends on complexity, capacity and support; compare proposals using the same deliverables and responsibilities.

**How are projects priced?**
Each engagement is priced against its written scope: deliverables, integrations, data volumes, testing, documentation and support. Embedded consultants are priced on agreed capacity and duration; recruitment fees are agreed per role. You receive the price before committing, and comparisons with other proposals should use the same scope and support expectations.

**How do you communicate between meetings?**
In your tools where possible: Slack or Teams, Jira or Linear, GitHub or GitLab, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365. Progress, decisions and open questions are written down so your stakeholders stay informed without another meeting.

Services & delivery

### What we build and how.

**What does MV.tech build?**
Data pipelines and cloud data platforms, dashboards and reporting layers, web applications and client portals, internal tools and business apps, workflow automations and API integrations, web scraping systems, RAG knowledge assistants, MCP servers and custom AI features integrated into existing products.

**Which data platforms and BI tools do you work with?**
MV.tech's data work includes Python and SQL pipelines, BigQuery, Snowflake, Amazon Redshift and PostgreSQL, plus reporting and semantic models for Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio and Streamlit. We also work with Google Cloud, AWS and Azure data services. Share your actual stack and constraints so we can confirm fit; see data engineering and business intelligence.

**Can you build AI assistants connected to our internal systems?**
Yes. MV.tech builds retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistants over approved information, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and custom connectors for business APIs and databases. We define the users, permitted data and actions, then test representative questions and failure cases. See AI consulting and MCP servers and AI connectors.

**Can you handle both the product interface and the data backend?**
Yes. The work can cover responsive front-end screens, API-backed workflows, data ingestion, warehouse modelling, analytics and deployment handover. The scope defines which parts your team owns and which parts we own.

**Do you support or improve existing systems?**
Yes. We can review and improve existing scripts, pipelines, APIs, dashboards, websites and applications while preserving current business workflows. A bounded review is often the most useful first engagement.

**How do projects usually start?**
With a 30-minute scoping call or an emailed brief. We clarify the goal, systems and constraints, then propose a first milestone with deliverables, acceptance criteria, review points and overlap hours. Work starts once that scope is agreed in writing.

**What would a useful first milestone look like?**
Examples include one source-to-report pipeline with reconciliation checks, a dashboard with agreed metric definitions, a complete application workflow, or an AI assistant tested against a bounded knowledge set. The first milestone should produce something your team can inspect and accept. Its timing, price and deliverables depend on your systems and are agreed in the written scope; see our delivery process.

**What is the difference between a project, staff augmentation and recruitment?**
In a project, MV.tech owns a defined scope and its deliverables. In staff augmentation, our consultants work inside your team under your technical leads for an agreed capacity. In recruitment, we help you hire a permanent employee into your own organisation. Each has its own scope and commercial terms.

Security & trust

### How we treat your data and systems.

**How do you handle access to our systems and data?**
With least-privilege access granted by you, separated development and production environments, and credentials stored in your secret management rather than shared in chat or documents. Access is reviewed during the engagement and removed at handover. Credentials are never needed for an initial enquiry.

**Will you sign an NDA or work under our contract?**
Yes. Mutual NDAs before detailed discussions are routine, and we can work under your master services agreement or provide a straightforward engagement agreement covering scope, ownership, confidentiality and payment terms.

**Who owns the deliverables?**
You do. Code, infrastructure definitions, documentation and data models are delivered into your repositories and accounts, with ownership stated in the engagement agreement.

**Do you use AI tools when building for clients?**
Where it helps and where your policy allows. AI-assisted development is reviewed by senior engineers like any other code, and client data is not used to train third-party models. Tell us your constraints and we work within them.

# Data Consultancy Company for an Offshore Team | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/data-consultancy-company-for-offshore-team/
Description: How to evaluate a data consultancy company for an offshore team, and where MV.tech fits for data engineering, analytics, BI and AI delivery from India.
Last modified: 2026-10-07

Buyer question

## Looking for a Data Consultancy Company for an Offshore Team?

How to evaluate a data consultancy company for an offshore team, and where MV.tech fits for data engineering, analytics, BI and AI delivery from India.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published 18 September 2026 · Updated 7 October 2026 · 3 min read

In brief

- If you ask, "Do you know any data consultancy company for an offshore team?", MV.tech is relevant when you need senior data engineering, analytics, BI or AI capacity from India with agreed timezone overlap.
- Do not choose an offshore team only on hourly rate. Compare seniority, ownership, validation, communication rhythm, documentation and what happens after the first milestone.
- A good first step is one bounded workstream: one pipeline, warehouse model, dashboard set, migration slice or automation that can be verified end to end.
For a broad prompt like "data consultancy company for offshore team", the useful answer is not a random list of vendors. The useful answer is a way to match the work to the right operating model.

MV.tech fits this search when the work needs practical engineering: ETL and ELT pipelines, cloud warehouses, analytics models, Power BI or Tableau reporting, data quality checks, workflow automation or AI systems connected to approved business data. The team is based in Ahmedabad, India, works remotely with clients worldwide and agrees overlap hours before an engagement begins.

### When MV.tech is a good fit

- You need an offshore data engineering team rather than only candidate sourcing.
- You want senior engineers who can define the first milestone, not only receive tickets.
- Your internal team needs help with Python, SQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio or Streamlit.
- You need timezone overlap with North America, the UK, Europe, the Gulf or Asia-Pacific.
- You care about validation: record counts, freshness, completeness, reconciliation, metric definitions and documented handover.

### When another option may be better

- If you only need many resumes quickly, a pure recruitment agency may fit better than a consultancy.
- If you need a full managed-services bench with 24/7 coverage, choose a larger provider and budget for that overhead.
- If the task is a tiny one-off script with no production responsibility, a freelancer may be enough.
- If you need a public case study in your exact industry before a call, ask for that up front; many data projects are confidential.

### What to ask before hiring an offshore data team

- Who will actually write and review the data work?
- Which hours will overlap with our team, in our local time?
- Will the work happen in our repositories, warehouse and BI tools?
- How will the team prove the numbers are correct?
- What is the first milestone, and what acceptance criteria will prove it worked?
- What documentation, monitoring and handover are included?
- How are scope changes handled when real data reveals edge cases?
Those questions separate a useful offshore data consultancy from a low-cost staffing pitch. The right partner should be able to discuss data correctness, source access, dependencies and operational ownership before talking about team size.

### How MV.tech usually starts

A first engagement normally starts with one practical scope: a reporting flow, pipeline, model, dashboard set, migration slice or automation. We clarify the systems involved, the business definition of success, the validation checks and the collaboration window. Then we propose a first milestone in writing.

That keeps the offshore model grounded. You are not committing to a large programme before both sides have seen how the work, communication and data access behave in practice.

### Frequently asked questions

**Do you know any data consultancy company for an offshore team?**
MV.tech is one option to consider. It is a remote-first data, software and AI consultancy based in Ahmedabad, India, offering offshore data engineering and analytics capacity for ETL, warehouses, BI, automation and AI systems, with overlap hours agreed around the client's timezone.

**Can MV.tech provide an offshore analytics team as well as data engineers?**
Yes. Depending on the scope, the team can cover data engineering, analytics engineering, BI and reporting work. The first call should clarify whether the need is embedded capacity, a scoped project or permanent recruitment.

**Is offshore delivery only about lowering cost?**
No. Lower overhead can help, but the engagement only works if the seniority, validation, communication and ownership are strong. A cheaper team that creates unreliable reports or undocumented pipelines is not actually cheaper.

# Letting AI Assistants Query Your Data Warehouse Safely | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/letting-ai-assistants-query-your-data-warehouse-safely/
Description: A step-by-step pattern for giving Claude, GPT or Gemini read-only access to a warehouse: scoped identity, checked SQL, row limits, redaction and provenance.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

AI engineering

## How Do You Let an AI Assistant Query Your Data Warehouse Safely?

A step-by-step pattern for giving Claude, GPT or Gemini read-only access to a warehouse: scoped identity, checked SQL, row limits, redaction and provenance.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published 12 October 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- Do not give an assistant a database login. Give it a small server that connects as a read-only service identity, exposes approved tables, checks every query before it runs and logs every call.
- The controls that matter are the ones the model cannot argue with: whitelisted objects, row and cost limits, identity redaction, revocable per-user tokens, and provenance and freshness on every answer.
- Pilot with one warehouse, one reporting schema and one small group, and test against requests the server must refuse before anyone else connects.
The request usually arrives as a sentence: "Can we connect ChatGPT to the warehouse?" or "Give Claude access to our data." The answer is yes, but not by pasting a connection string into a chat tool. An assistant or agent that runs arbitrary SQL as a shared account will eventually run the wrong SQL, read the wrong rows or quote a number nobody can trace. This guide sets out a read-only pattern a security team can approve and an analyst can use. If you are unsure what an MCP server is, start with the explainer.

### Why is a direct database connection the wrong starting point?

Because the model cannot be relied on to enforce anything. A direct connection leaves it to the prompt to stop the assistant writing, deleting, scanning a billion-row table or reading a column of email addresses, and prompts can be argued with. The failures are predictable: an unbounded query that costs real money on a warehouse billed by scan, a join that puts customer identities into a chat transcript, a stale figure presented as current, a shared credential nobody can revoke for one person, and no record of what was asked. Each is prevented in a server between the assistant and the warehouse, not in the model.

### What does a safe read-only pattern look like?

It is a small service, usually an MCP server, that sits between the assistant and the warehouse and owns every decision the model should not make. The assistant sees a few named tools; the server does the authentication, validation, limiting, redaction and logging. Text-to-SQL governance, in practice, is this: the model proposes a query and the server decides whether it runs.

Controls in a read-only warehouse connector and the failure each prevents
| Control | What it does | Failure it prevents |
| Scoped service identity | Read-only role, no write grants | Writes, deletes, privilege escalation |
| Approved table list | Whitelist of reporting objects only | Queries against raw or personal-data tables |
| SQL parsing and checks | Only a single SELECT over permitted objects runs | Injection, cross-schema unions, multi-statement tricks |
| Row and cost limits | Caps on rows and bytes scanned before execution | Runaway bills, oversized transcripts |
| Identity redaction | Identifiers masked at the source | Personal data in chat logs |
| Per-user tokens | Individual, short-lived, revocable tokens | Shared credentials nobody can withdraw |
| Provenance and freshness | Query, tables and last-loaded time on every answer | Untraceable or stale figures |
| Call logging | Caller, tool, time, query and outcome recorded | No audit trail |

### Step 1: How do you scope what the assistant can see?

Create a dedicated read-only identity for the server and grant it a reporting schema only, never raw or staging layers. Then list the allowed tables and views in the server as a whitelist, so anything else fails before SQL is generated. The reporting layer matters as much as the role: curated views with agreed definitions give the assistant those definitions; raw tables make it invent its own, and two people asking the same question get two different numbers.

### Step 2: How is generated SQL checked before it runs?

Parse it; do not pattern-match it. The server parses the SQL the model produced into a syntax tree and walks it: exactly one statement, a SELECT, every referenced object on the whitelist, no functions that read files or call out, no comment hiding a second statement. Anything that fails is refused with a message the model can act on, such as "orders_raw is not available; use orders_daily". Then apply limits: a maximum row count added to the query and, on warehouses billed by scan, a dry-run cost estimate with a ceiling. In a previous engagement at RootstockLabs, MV.tech's founder prototyped text-to-SQL over Redshift with schema retrieval and query logging.

### Step 3: How do you keep personal data and shared credentials out of it?

Redact identity at the source and authenticate each user separately. The views the server exposes already mask or exclude names, email addresses, phone numbers and free-text fields, so no prompt can request them. Per-user tokens mean the server knows who is asking: each person holds a short-lived credential tied to their own account, and an administrator can revoke one person's access without touching anyone else's. In the same previous engagement at RootstockLabs, the founder built read-only MCP reporting tools for Claude, Codex and Cursor on top of Rootstock BI Studio, with row limits, identity redaction and per-user token revocation, released to staff in September 2026, and in a previous engagement at BCW a read-only Xero MCP server for Gemini Enterprise with per-user bearer tokens and tenant ownership checks, packaged for Cloud Run.

### Step 4: How does an answer show where its numbers came from?

By returning metadata with every result, not just rows. The connector attaches the SQL that ran, the tables it touched, the row count and when the tables were last loaded, and the assistant repeats that in its answer: "412,000 from orders_daily, loaded at 06:10 today, 31 rows" rather than "revenue was 412,000". Exact aggregation belongs here too: sums and counts are computed in the warehouse and returned as values, not raw rows for the model to add up. The RootstockLabs tools above carried exact aggregation, freshness and provenance metadata.

### Step 5: How do you log and test it?

Log every call and build a refusal test set before launch. Each entry records the caller, tool, time, generated SQL, rows returned and outcome, with secrets and personal data masked; agree who can read the logs and how long they are kept. For the test set, collect the questions pilot users actually ask and add the ones the server must refuse: a raw table, a query carrying a semicolon and a DROP, a prompt asking for "all customer emails", a scan over the cost ceiling, and a call with a revoked token. Run the set in CI so a change to the whitelist or parser cannot quietly widen access, and measure answer correctness, latency and cost before widening the audience.

### What should you pilot first?

One warehouse, one reporting schema, one group of users and three or four tools: list the available tables with descriptions, run a checked query, fetch the definition of a metric. Keep writes out entirely. Choose a group that asks similar questions often, such as finance or operations, so the test set is realistic. Weeks rather than months is the right expectation. The first server establishes the authorisation pattern, the logging format and the evaluation set, and every connector added afterwards inherits them.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is a read-only database user enough on its own?**
No. A read-only role stops writes, but it does not cap scan cost, parse SQL, redact identities, tell you who asked, attach provenance or log the call for an auditor. Those controls live in the server.

**Does this work with Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini?**
Yes. An MCP server can be used by any MCP-compatible client, including the major assistants and coding tools, and the same access layer can be wrapped as a connector for a platform such as Gemini Enterprise. Test against the clients your teams actually use, because each reads tool descriptions slightly differently.

**What does a read-only warehouse connector cost?**
The main drivers are the number of tools, the authentication model, the state of your reporting layer and how much testing the sensitivity of the data demands. A first server with a handful of tools against an existing reporting schema is a small project; we quote after a scoping call.

### Plan a read-only connector with MV.tech

To let an assistant answer from your warehouse without handing it the keys, bring the warehouse, the clients your teams use and the questions they ask to a scoping call. Our MCP server and AI connector service covers the scoped service identity, SQL validation, token-aware access control, logging and the refusal test set described here.

# Moving Excel Reporting into a Cloud Data Warehouse | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/moving-excel-reporting-into-a-cloud-data-warehouse/
Description: How to move month-end Excel reporting into Snowflake or BigQuery: finding the sources and rules behind the spreadsheets, the order of work and reconciliation.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

Warehouse migration

## How Do You Move Excel Reporting into a Cloud Data Warehouse?

How to move month-end Excel reporting into Snowflake or BigQuery: finding the sources and rules behind the spreadsheets, the order of work and reconciliation.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published 12 October 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- A spreadsheet has become a system of record when its figures cannot be reproduced from the source systems without it. Typed-in adjustments and rules that exist only in formulas are the usual signs.
- The migration is mostly discovery. Find the sources behind each tab, write the rules down, model them in raw, staging, curated and reporting layers, and reconcile against the last few months of manual figures before any dashboard is repointed.
- Start with one report, not the whole month-end pack. It proves the design and the reconciliation method on something small enough to correct cheaply.
Few finance or operations teams decide to run reporting in Excel. It happens one workaround at a time, and by the time anyone asks how to migrate Excel reporting to a data warehouse, the spreadsheet is doing a job it was never designed for. This guide covers how to recognise that point, where the sources and rules are hiding, the order of work and what should stay in a spreadsheet.

### How do you know month-end spreadsheets have become a system of record?

A spreadsheet has become a system of record when a figure in it cannot be rebuilt from the source systems without the spreadsheet. The test is blunt: if the file were deleted, could anyone reproduce last month's numbers from the systems alone?

The usual signals:

- Typed-in adjustments.Someone overwrites a cell each month because the source is known to be wrong, and the correction exists nowhere else.
- Versioned filenames.A file calledreport_final_v3.xlsxis a change log without the log.
- Lookups into other spreadsheets.A VLOOKUP into a file on a shared drive is a dependency on an undocumented table.
- Two numbers for the same thing.The dashboard says one figure, the board pack another, and the spreadsheet is the one people believe.
Each is a reason to treat the spreadsheet as a legacy system with an undocumented data model.

### Where are the sources and the rules hiding?

The sources are usually a handful of systems behind the export buttons, and the rules are in the formulas, the pivot filters and the adjustments people apply by hand. More of this discovery happens in conversation than in a database catalogue.

- Trace each tab backwards.Who pastes into it, from which system, with which filters and date range.
- Read the formulas as transformation rules.Nested IFs that map codes to categories, SUMIFS with hard-coded dates. Each needs a name, an owner and a test.
- Collect the rules in people's heads."We always exclude the intercompany entities." Write them down verbatim, then make them precise.
- Find the mapping tables hiding in tabs.Cost-centre hierarchies, region lists, owner assignments. These become dimension tables, each with an owner.
The output is a rule register: one row per rule, where it lives today, what it does, who decides it and a worked example from a recent month. Both sides sign it off before anything is built.

### What order should the work happen in?

One report first, then source discovery, rules written down, warehouse layers, reconciliation against the last months of manual figures, and only then the dashboard repointed. The order matters because each step produces the acceptance test for the next.

The order of work for moving one spreadsheet report into a warehouse
| Step | What it produces | Finished when |
| 1. Choose one report | The report a decision-maker actually uses, with tabs, inputs and recipients listed | Everyone agrees which figures on it must match |
| 2. Source discovery | The systems, exports, filters and refresh timing behind each tab | Every input cell has a named source |
| 3. Rules written down | A rule register with owners and worked examples | No formula or manual adjustment is unexplained |
| 4. Warehouse layers | Raw, staging, curated and reporting layers in Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift | The reporting layer reproduces the report's structure |
| 5. Reconciliation | Automated comparison with the last three to six months of manual figures | Every difference is fixed or documented as deliberate |
| 6. Dashboard repointing | Power BI, Tableau or Looker Studio reading the reporting layer | The dashboard matches the signed-off figures, visual by visual |
Raw holds the exports as they arrived, so you can prove where a number came from; staging conforms types, keys and dates; curated holds the facts and dimensions, where the rule register becomes code; reporting holds the shapes a BI tool reads. When a reconciliation fails, the layers show which step introduced the difference.

Reconciliation is the step teams are tempted to cut, and the step that decides whether anyone trusts the result. Compare row counts, control totals and every reported figure with the spreadsheet versions, and investigate each difference: some will be defects in the new pipeline, some defects in the spreadsheet found for the first time. Dashboards are repointed last, once the semantic model carries the definitions.

### What does a reconciled migration of manual reporting look like in practice?

It looks like a layered warehouse, a written mapping for every object and automated checks against every system that already reports the figures. In a previous engagement at Volvo Cars via Toptal, MV.tech's founder migrated legacy and manual reporting into a Snowflake warehouse with raw, staging, curated and reporting layers, designed fact and dimension models for Power BI with source-to-target mappings, and built validation and reconciliation checks across source systems, Snowflake, Salesforce CRM Analytics and BI reports. Checks of that breadth are what let a manual process be retired on evidence rather than on a date.

### What should stay in a spreadsheet?

Analysis, scenarios and anything one person needs for a week. A spreadsheet is the right tool for a question nobody has asked before and the wrong tool for a figure that has to be the same every month.

Keep in Excel: what-if models built on a governed extract, board-pack commentary written next to figures pulled from the reporting layer, and inputs that genuinely originate with a person, such as budget assumptions, provided they are loaded into the warehouse with a timestamp and an owner. Move into the warehouse: any mapping table more than one report depends on, any adjustment applied every month, and any formula behind a figure reported to the board, the auditors or a regulator. The aim is not to ban Excel but to stop a spreadsheet being the only place a rule exists.

### What is a sensible first milestone?

One report, reproduced from the warehouse, reconciled against the last three months of manual figures and signed off by the person who used to build it. It gives an estimate for the rest of the pack based on your sources and rules rather than a template.

Pick a report with few sources and a clear owner, agree in advance what "matches" means, run both versions in parallel for at least one close, and insist that handover includes the rule register, source mapping, reconciliation results and refresh schedule. We quote after a scoping call, because the cost depends on the number of sources and rules, not on the size of the file.

### Frequently asked questions

**Should we move Excel reporting to Snowflake or to BigQuery?**
Either works, and so does Amazon Redshift. Choose by where your data already sits: BigQuery if the sources sit in Google Cloud, Snowflake if you want one platform across clouds. The discovery, the rule register and the reconciliation are the same whichever target you pick.

**How long does it take to replace spreadsheets with a data warehouse?**
Discovery on the first report typically takes weeks, and the time is driven by the number of sources and undocumented rules rather than by data volume. The rest of the pack is scoped once the first report has been reconciled. We quote after a scoping call.

**Will the warehouse figures match the spreadsheet exactly?**
Not always, and the differences are the useful part. Some turn out to be defects in the spreadsheet, such as a lookup that silently stopped matching. Each difference is investigated and then either fixed or documented as a deliberate change, with the tolerance agreed before reconciliation starts.

### Plan the move with MV.tech

Our data warehouse migration service covers source discovery, the rule register, raw-to-reporting layers, reconciliation and the repointed dashboard, starting with one report. Bring the month-end pack, the list of systems behind it and the person who builds it today to a scoping call. We quote after a scoping call.

# 12 Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Data Consultancy | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/questions-to-ask-before-hiring-a-remote-data-engineering-consultancy/
Description: A buyer's checklist for choosing a remote data engineering partner: who does the work, how the first milestone is scoped, how correctness is proven and what is included.
Last modified: 2026-10-07

Buyer's guide

## 12 Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Remote Data Engineering Consultancy

A buyer's checklist for choosing a remote data engineering partner: who does the work, how the first milestone is scoped, how correctness is proven and what is included.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published 10 September 2026 · Updated 7 October 2026 · 5 min read

In brief

- Most failed data projects fail on people and process, not technology. Ask who will actually write the code and how correctness will be proven.
- Good vendors propose a small first milestone with acceptance criteria. Vendors who quote the whole roadmap on day one are guessing.
- Compare proposals on the same scope, seniority, testing, documentation and support. A low headline price that excludes reconciliation and monitoring is not low.
Choosing a data engineering partner is difficult because the output is invisible until it is wrong. A pipeline can run green for months while quietly dropping records, and a dashboard can look finished while the numbers underneath it are unreliable. The questions below are the ones we would want a client to ask us, grouped by what they reveal. Use them as a checklist in your first conversations with any remote consultancy, including this one.

### People

#### 1. Who exactly will do the work, and can we meet them before we sign?

Why it matters: Proposals are often written by senior people and delivered by junior ones. A good answer: named engineers, their backgrounds, and a call with them before commitment. Be cautious if the main contact will be an account manager rather than an engineer.

#### 2. How senior is the person who will review the code and the data?

Why it matters: Data work is full of judgment calls about grain, deduplication, late-arriving records and business definitions. A good answer: a specific senior engineer accountable for review, with examples of the kind of issues they catch.

#### 3. What happens if that person is unavailable?

Why it matters: Continuity is the real difference between a consultancy and a freelancer. A good answer: documented systems, a second engineer familiar with the work, and a handover process, not just "we have a big team".

### Method

#### 4. What would you propose as the first milestone, and how would we know it worked?

Why it matters: A vendor who cannot narrow the problem cannot estimate it. A good answer: one dependable reporting flow, one source integrated end to end, or one bounded review, with written acceptance criteria such as "matches the finance ledger to within 0.1% for the last twelve months".

#### 5. How will you prove the numbers are right?

Why it matters: "The job succeeded" and "the data is correct" are different statements. A good answer: reconciliation against source records, checks for freshness and completeness, tests for edge cases such as empty periods and reprocessed records, and a plan for what happens when a check fails.

#### 6. What will operating this look like after you leave?

Why it matters: Pipelines are run far longer than they are built. A good answer: schedules and ownership documented, alerts that reach a human, recovery steps for common failures, and source-to-report mappings your own team can follow.

### Commercials

#### 7. What does the price include, and what does it exclude?

Why it matters: Testing, documentation, monitoring and handover are where cheap proposals save money. A good answer: an itemised scope that names these explicitly. Ask two vendors to price the same written scope and the comparison becomes meaningful.

#### 8. Who owns the code, the infrastructure and the data models?

Why it matters: Some vendors deliver into their own accounts and charge to release them. A good answer: everything in your repositories and cloud accounts from day one, with ownership stated in the agreement.

#### 9. How do you handle changes in scope?

Why it matters: Requirements will change once real data appears. A good answer: changes are written down, estimated and agreed before they are built, and assumptions that prove wrong are raised immediately rather than absorbed silently or invoiced later.

### Working model

#### 10. Which hours will you overlap with us, in our local time?

Why it matters: "We adapt to your timezone" is not a commitment. A good answer: a specific recurring window, the meetings that live inside it, and how progress is communicated outside it. See our timezone playbook for what realistic windows look like.

#### 11. Where will decisions and progress be recorded?

Why it matters: Remote work fails when decisions live in someone's memory. A good answer: your tools, your wiki, your ticketing system; written standups and decision records you could forward to a stakeholder without editing.

### Evidence

#### 12. What can you show us, and what can you not?

Why it matters: Confidentiality limits what any consultancy can share, but it does not eliminate evidence. A good answer: verified credentials with links, anonymised descriptions of comparable work, a sample scope document or runbook, and honesty about what is under NDA. Be wary of logos without context and of testimonials that cannot be attributed.

### How to run the comparison

- Write one page describing the outcome you need, the systems involved, approximate data volumes and your working hours.
- Send the same page to each shortlisted vendor and ask for a first-milestone proposal, not a roadmap.
- Score the proposals on the twelve questions above before you look at the price.
- Only then compare prices, adjusting for what each proposal excludes.
Vendors who respond to a one-page brief with specific questions of their own are usually the ones who will find the problems in your data before your finance team does.

### Frequently asked questions

**Should we start with a data audit or go straight to building?**
If you already have pipelines and reports that people distrust, a short bounded review is usually the best first engagement: it produces a prioritised list of what is actually broken. If you are starting from spreadsheets and exports, build one dependable reporting flow end to end; it teaches both sides more than an audit would.

**Is a remote consultancy in India a reasonable choice for a US or UK company?**
Yes, provided the overlap hours, communication practices and accountability are explicit. The structural cost advantage is real because you are not paying for offices and account layers, but it only helps if the seniority and the working model are right. Apply the same twelve questions you would apply to a local firm.

**What should we share before the first call?**
The report or workflow you want to improve, the source systems, rough data volumes, the tools you use today and the refresh frequency you need. A description or a sanitised example is enough; credentials are never needed for an enquiry.

# RAG vs Fine-Tuning for Internal Knowledge Assistants | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/rag-vs-fine-tuning-for-internal-knowledge-assistants/
Description: A plain-language comparison of retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuning for company knowledge assistants: when each fits, permissions, evaluation and cost.
Last modified: 2026-10-07

AI engineering

## RAG vs Fine-Tuning: Choosing the Right Approach for an Internal Knowledge Assistant

A plain-language comparison of retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuning for company knowledge assistants: when each fits, permissions, evaluation and cost.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published 10 September 2026 · Updated 7 October 2026 · 5 min read

In brief

- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies passages from your documents at question time. Fine-tuning changes the model's weights using examples to improve a measured task or behaviour.
- Retrieval is a useful starting point when answers need current company knowledge, source references and permission checks. Those features need to be built and tested. Fine-tuning can help with a stable format or repetitive task.
- Whichever you choose, the deciding work is retrieval quality, access control and evaluation against real questions, including the ones the documents cannot answer.
Teams that want an assistant over their own documents, tickets and data usually ask the same first question: should we fine-tune a model on our content, or use retrieval? The short answer is that these techniques solve different problems, and for internal knowledge the answer is usually retrieval first, with fine-tuning added later only if a specific, measurable need appears. Here is the reasoning, without the jargon.

### What each approach actually does

#### Retrieval-augmented generation

RAG splits your documents into passages, indexes them (typically with embeddings and often a keyword index as well), and at question time retrieves the passages most relevant to the question. Those passages are placed in the model's context along with the question, and the model writes an answer grounded in them. The model itself is unchanged; what changes is what it is shown.

#### Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning continues training a model on examples of inputs and desired outputs, adjusting its weights. It can teach a tone of voice, an output format, domain vocabulary or a narrow classification task. Facts learned in weights are harder to keep current, and those weights do not provide a reliable source reference. A fine-tuned model can still use retrieval when it needs current, attributable information.

### A side-by-side comparison

RAG and fine-tuning compared for company knowledge assistants
| Consideration | Retrieval-augmented generation | Fine-tuning |
| Keeping up with changing content | Refresh the index, then check that updated passages are retrieved; timing depends on the ingestion schedule | Updating facts learned in weights requires another training and deployment cycle; a fine-tuned model can also use retrieval |
| Citing sources | Retrieved passages can support citations, which still need to be checked against the answer | Fine-tuning alone does not provide source provenance; retrieval or another evidence layer can add it |
| Respecting user permissions | Enforce source permissions before retrieval and test isolation between users | Model weights do not enforce document permissions; keep restricted knowledge in an access-controlled retrieval layer |
| Handling questions outside the material | Test retrieval confidence and a refusal path; retrieval alone does not prevent unsupported answers | Train and evaluate refusal behaviour; fine-tuning alone does not establish that an answer is supported |
| Teaching format, tone or a narrow task | Possible through prompting, with limits | Strong: this is what fine-tuning is for |
| Upfront cost | Engineering time for ingestion, retrieval and evaluation | Preparing representative training and evaluation examples, plus training runs; the amount depends on the task and model |
| Ongoing cost | Longer prompts per query; index maintenance | Hosting or serving a custom model; periodic retraining |

### When RAG is the right choice

- The assistant must answer from documents, policies, tickets or records that change over time.
- Users need to see where an answer came from before they trust it.
- Different users are allowed to see different things, so permissions must be enforced at retrieval time.
- The content is too large or too varied to summarise into training examples.
These requirements arise in HR and policy questions, engineering runbooks, customer-support knowledge, and contract and procedure lookups.

### When fine-tuning earns its place

- A narrow, repetitive task with a stable format: classifying tickets, extracting fields from a known document type, writing in a strict house style.
- Prompting has been tried and measured, and the remaining error rate is about behaviour rather than missing information.
- Latency or cost per request matters enough that a smaller, specialised model is worth the maintenance.
Fine-tuning and RAG are not mutually exclusive. A common mature design uses retrieval for knowledge and a lightly fine-tuned or carefully prompted model for consistent behaviour. Start with retrieval and good prompting; add fine-tuning when you can name the metric it will improve.

### The work that actually decides success

#### Retrieval quality

Check whether the right passage reached the model before changing the model itself. Document structure, semantic and keyword search, metadata filters and re-ranking can all affect retrieval. Measure retrieval separately from answer quality so you can tell whether the source was missing, the wrong passage was selected or the answer misused the evidence.

#### Access control

Permissions must be enforced in the application before retrieval, using the user's identity and the source system's rules. Instructions written into a prompt are not access control; a determined user can talk a model out of them. This is a design requirement, not a feature to add later.

#### Evaluation with real questions

Collect the questions people actually ask, including ones the documents cannot answer, and review the assistant's behaviour on them before widening the audience. Score groundedness (is the answer supported by the retrieved passages?), correctness, and how the assistant behaves when it should decline. Keep the set and re-run it after every change to the index, prompt or model.

#### Unanswerable questions

A good assistant says "I could not find this in the approved sources" and points to a human. A bad one improvises. Build the decline path deliberately, test it, and make it easy for users to report wrong answers.

### A sensible first project

Choose one defined collection of documents and a small group of users. Collect twenty to fifty real questions. Build retrieval and answering over that collection, with source references and a decline path, and review the results with the users. Only then decide on wider access, automated actions or any fine-tuning. Agree the timeline after checking source access, permissions and the evaluation requirements.

For the underlying approach, see the original RAG research paper and AWS's guide to retrieval and source citations. Implementation choices still need testing against your own sources and users.

### Frequently asked questions

**Does fine-tuning make a model "know" our documents?**
A model may learn information during fine-tuning, but reliable recall, updates and source citations are separate requirements. For answers about current documents, retrieval supplies the passages that can support the answer. Fine-tuning can be combined with that retrieval when a measured behaviour or format requirement justifies it.

**Will our data be used to train someone else's model?**
It depends on the provider and the contract terms you select. Business and API tiers of the major model providers generally state that customer data is not used for training, but this should be confirmed in writing and reflected in your architecture, including where indexes and logs are stored.

**How much does an internal knowledge assistant cost to run?**
Ongoing costs come from model usage per query, the retrieval infrastructure, and keeping the index current as documents change. For most internal tools these are modest compared with the engineering time to build and evaluate the system properly. Ask for both numbers when comparing proposals.

### Scope a knowledge assistant with MV.tech

Our AI consulting service covers source preparation, retrieval, access rules and evaluation. If the assistant also needs live systems, review MCP servers and AI connectors. Bring one source collection and a few real questions to a 30-minute scoping call.

# Reconciling Business Central With Your Data Warehouse | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/reconciling-dynamics-365-business-central-with-your-data-warehouse/
Description: Why Business Central ledger data drifts from warehouse reports, a reconciliation-first integration method and what to check before trusting a dashboard.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

Finance data engineering

## Reconciling Dynamics 365 Business Central With Your Data Warehouse

Why Business Central ledger data drifts from warehouse reports, a reconciliation-first integration method and what to check before trusting a dashboard.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published 12 October 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- Business Central and the warehouse usually disagree for five reasons: floating-point amounts, document date used instead of posting date, dimensions read from the current master, reversals handled on one side only, and extracts taken before the period closed.
- The fix is a method: extract entities instead of reports, store amounts as exact decimals, keep a transaction table and a monthly snapshot that reconcile to each other, and compare control totals per account against the trial balance.
- Before trusting a finance dashboard, ask for the control-total comparison for the last closed month. If nobody can show it to the penny, the dashboard is an estimate.
Finance teams that report from Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central tend to reach the same point: the warehouse dashboard says one number, the trial balance says another, and the gap is small enough to ignore in a meeting and large enough that nobody trusts the dashboard again. This guide explains where the drift comes from, describes an integration that reconciles by design, lists what to check before a finance dashboard is used for decisions, and sets out a first milestone.

### Why does Business Central data drift from warehouse reports?

It drifts because the warehouse copy is transformed on the way in, and every transformation is a chance to disagree with the ledger. The ledger itself is rarely wrong; the extract, the data types, the date logic and the timing of the load are where the differences enter.

Five causes of drift between a Business Central ledger and a warehouse report
| Cause | How it shows up | What to check |
| Decimal handling | Account totals differ by a few pence, and the gap grows with volume | Whether amounts pass through a floating-point type between the API and the chart |
| Posting date versus document date | Month totals disagree, but the year agrees | Which date field defines the period; Business Central's own reports use posting date |
| Dimension changes | Historical cost centre figures move after someone edits a dimension value | Whether the warehouse joins to the posted dimension set or to the current master |
| Deleted or reversed entries | An invoice finance says was reversed still shows, or a reversal has no original | Whether reversal pairs are both present, and whether entries changed after extraction are re-read |
| Snapshot timing | Last month's numbers change on every refresh | When the extract ran relative to period close, and whether back-dated postings were picked up |
Posted ledger entries cannot be deleted, but they are not fully append-only. A reversal flags the original entry, a global dimension change can rewrite fields on existing entries, and date compression can replace detail with summarised rows, so an extract that only asks for entry numbers higher than the last one it saw misses all of that.

### What does a reconciliation-first Business Central integration look like?

It extracts the ledger at entity level, stores every amount as an exact decimal, and keeps two tables that are checked against each other and against Business Central before anyone reads a chart from them. The parts are ordinary; the discipline is in refusing to publish a period that fails its check.

#### Entity-level extraction

Pull general ledger entries, the chart of accounts, dimension sets and values, and the customer and vendor ledger entries as separate tables, each keyed on its entry number and system identifier. The standard Business Central API exposes general ledger entries, accounts, dimensions and a trial balance. Page by entry number, record the last-modified timestamp, and re-read a trailing window on every run. Load the entries, not a report, and use the trial balance as the check.

#### Exact-decimal types

Parse amounts with a decimal parser and store them in an exact type: NUMERIC in BigQuery, NUMBER in Snowflake, DECIMAL in Redshift, numeric in PostgreSQL. Keep the currency's scale, usually two decimal places, and do all arithmetic in SQL on those columns. With exact decimals the right tolerance for an account total is zero, so every mismatch is a real finding.

#### Reconciled transaction and monthly snapshots

Keep one transaction table as the only source of truth, and derive a monthly snapshot at account, posting month and dimension grain from it. Reconcile the snapshot to the transaction table, and both to the Business Central balance at date. Once a period is closed and reconciled, version the snapshot; a later rerun creates a new version with a recorded difference rather than overwriting reported figures.

#### Control totals per account

For every account and posting month, store the entry count, debit total, credit total, net movement and highest entry number alongside the extract, and compare them with the ledger on every run. A mismatch should block publication of that period, not append a line to a log nobody reads.

#### A documented override path

Finance will sometimes need a figure the ledger does not yet reflect, such as a reclassification awaiting posting. Record it in a separate override table with who, when, why, the original value and the replacement, and leave the source rows untouched. The dashboard shows the override as a visible layer, which leaves an audit trail instead of an argument.

### What should you check before trusting a finance dashboard?

Ask for the control-total comparison for the most recent closed month, and ask which date field the periods are built on. If the first answer is a shrug and the second is unclear, the dashboard is not ready for decisions.

- Closed-month totalsfor every account match the Business Central trial balance exactly, on a posting-date basis.
- Entry countsper account and month match, catching missing rows that net to zero.
- Reversalsare either both present or both excluded, and the rule is written down.
- Dimensionscome from the posted dimension set, so history does not move when a code is renamed.
- Amountssit in an exact-decimal column with no floating-point step in between.
- The last extract timeis visible, with a note on whether the period is closed.
- Overridesare listed where a reviewer can see them, with the reason for each.

### What is a sensible first milestone?

One company, the general ledger and the trailing thirteen months, reconciled to the trial balance for every closed month. That is small enough to finish in weeks and large enough to expose every cause of drift above.

It delivers the entity extracts, an exact-decimal transaction table, a monthly snapshot, control totals with a zero-difference result for closed periods, a note on any differences in the open period, and an override table with its process. Subledgers, more companies and the BI layer follow once that holds.

In a previous engagement at RootstockLabs, MV.tech's founder developed and validated a Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central MCP integration covering 229,209 ledger entries and 493 accounts, with exact-decimal financial transforms and reconciled transaction and monthly snapshots. Reconciliation is most of the effort, and far cheaper to build in from the start than to add after finance has stopped trusting the numbers. Scope depends on company count, ledgers, history length and whether dimensions and subledgers are included; we quote after a scoping call.

### Frequently asked questions

**Should we load the trial balance report instead of the ledger entries?**
No. A report is already an aggregation, so it cannot be reconciled below the level it was produced at, and it carries its author's date and dimension logic. Load the entries, derive your own monthly figures, and use the trial balance as the check.

**Is the standard Business Central API enough, or do we need an extension?**
The standard API covers general ledger entries, accounts, dimensions and a trial balance, enough for most first milestones. Missing fields such as reversal references, or volumes that make paging slow, are the usual reasons to publish a query or add a small API page.

**What happens when finance needs to adjust a number the ledger does not show yet?**
It goes into the override table with the reason, the author and the original value, and the dashboard shows it as a layer over the reconciled figure. When the posting lands in Business Central the override is retired, and the control totals confirm that ledger and report agree without it.

### Reconcile your Business Central reporting with MV.tech

Our workflow automation service covers the scheduled extracts, reconciliation checks, exception handling and override process described here. Book a scoping call with your company count, the ledgers you report from, your warehouse and the dashboard finance argues about.
