### Questions people ask before hiring a data engineer.

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**How much does it cost to hire a data engineer from India?**
We quote after a scoping call. The figure depends on the role, seniority, allocated capacity, duration and the support expected outside overlap hours, so a number before that conversation would be a guess. MV.tech's remote model keeps office and account-management overhead out of the price, and we ask you to compare proposals on the same scope, seniority and support expectations.

**Can a remote team in India work in our timezone?**
Yes. India Standard Time overlaps every major business region for part of the day, and we agree the window in your local time before the engineer starts. Typical windows are 9:00 am to 1:00 pm US Eastern, 7:00 to 10:00 am US Pacific, 9:00 am to 3:30 pm in the UK, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm in Central Europe, most of the day in the Gulf and 12:30 to 6:00 pm in eastern Australia. Overlap does not mean round-the-clock support; any out-of-hours coverage is written into the scope separately.

**Can we hire a fractional or part-time data engineer?**
Yes. A fractional arrangement of a few days a week suits a small team that needs senior judgement on pipelines, warehouse modelling or BI without a full-time hire. The capacity, the days and the overlap hours are agreed up front, and the engineer stays the same person for the duration rather than whoever is free that week.

**Will we get a named engineer or a bench?**
A named engineer. You meet the person before anything is signed, review their experience against your stack and work with them directly for the duration. If the engagement grows into a team, composition, start dates and availability are confirmed during scoping rather than implied by the website.

**What is the difference between staff augmentation, a scoped project and recruitment?**
With staff augmentation the engineer works inside your team under your leads' direction for an agreed capacity and duration. With a scoped project MV.tech owns a defined deliverable, its acceptance criteria and handover. With technology recruitment you hire a permanent employee into your own organisation and agree employment terms with them directly. We clarify which arrangement you need before discussing candidates or consultants.

**How does a trial milestone reduce the risk of hiring remotely?**
Because you judge delivered work rather than an interview. The first milestone is small, written down and checkable: a pipeline that reconciles to the source, a model whose figures match the ones people report, a dashboard with documented definitions. If the result or the working relationship is not right, the engagement ends at the review with the work and its documentation handed over.

**What should we share before asking to hire a data engineer?**
The workstream or backlog, the source systems and target warehouse or BI tools, the skills you need, the expected duration and capacity, your timezone and the hours that matter, and any constraints around security or access. A sanitised example of the data is enough for the first call; credentials are never needed for an enquiry.

# Custom MCP Server Development for Safe AI Database Access | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/services/mcp-and-ai-connectors/
Description: Custom MCP servers and AI connectors in Python: scoped, validated and logged access to your databases, APIs and tools, delivered remotely from India.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

Service · Remote-first senior specialists

## Custom MCP servers and AI connectors for scoped, logged access to your systems

Give an AI agent access to real systems without handing over the keys. MV.tech builds custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and AI connectors in Python that expose approved databases, APIs and internal tools to enterprise AI platforms, with scoped authorisation, validated queries, logged calls and evaluation before access is widened.

- Remote from Ahmedabad, India
- Overlap with your timezone
- Senior specialists, direct access
- Scope agreed in writing
The starting point

### When does a business need a custom MCP server or AI connector?

- An assistant is convincing in a demo but has no safe route to live data.
- Your enterprise AI platform has a connector for everything except the system the business runs on.
- Analysts want questions answered from a governed dataset, with the generated SQL checked before it runs.
- Several teams are each building their own prompt-and-paste workflow against the same internal tools.
- Security will not approve an agent that authenticates as a shared admin account.
- An agent can already read your data and nobody can produce an audit trail of what it read.
- A working MCP prototype now needs authentication, error handling, logging and a deployment story.
What we deliver

### What does MCP server and AI connector development include?

01

#### Custom MCP servers in Python

Model Context Protocol servers built around your systems: tool definitions with typed inputs, explicit failure modes, resources, pagination and sensible limits. Tools are designed around tasks a person would recognise rather than mirroring every API endpoint, because an agent chooses far better from a short, well-named list.

02

#### Connectors and plugins for enterprise AI platforms

Connectors, plugins and extensions for the AI platforms your organisation has already adopted — including Claude, Gemini Enterprise and Cortex AI environments — so approved data reaches assistants through one maintained integration instead of several ad-hoc ones.

03

#### Database, API and internal-tool access

Connect agents to warehouses, operational databases, REST APIs, ticketing and finance systems. Access runs through a scoped service identity against an approved set of tables or endpoints: read-only by default, whitelists rather than blocklists, and no path to anything outside the agreed surface.

04

#### Secure retrieval, SQL generation and validation

Where an agent generates SQL, it generates it against a governed reporting layer. Queries are parsed and checked before execution — permitted objects only, row and cost limits, no writes — and results are validated and shaped before they are returned. Retrieval respects the permissions the requesting user already has.

05

#### OAuth, secrets and token-aware access control

Authorisation designed into the integration: OAuth flows, short-lived tokens, secrets held in a managed store such as Secret Manager, and per-user identity carried through to the data layer. Log the caller, tool, time and outcome; include only approved argument fields, mask secrets and personal data, and agree log access and retention for the audit trail.

06

#### Reusable AI skills and packaged workflows

Package the sequences people repeat — retrieve, generate SQL, validate, format, export — as reusable skills and tools rather than prompts copied between teams, so behaviour is versioned, tested and improved in one place.

07

#### Evaluation, guardrails and deployment

Agree a test set of real requests, including ones the server should refuse, and measure tool-selection accuracy, answer correctness, latency and cost before widening access. Ship containerised with Pytest coverage, CI, structured logging and a documented upgrade path as the protocol and the clients change.

A useful first project

### What does a first custom MCP server project look like?

Choose one system your teams query constantly and one small group of users. Define the three or four tools that cover most of their requests, wire them to a scoped service identity, and put validation and logging around every call from the first day. Test against the requests those users actually make, including the ones the server should refuse. That first server establishes the authorisation pattern, the logging format and the evaluation set, and every connector added afterwards inherits them instead of reinventing them.

- 03 — Deploy and maintain — Ship with logging, monitoring and CI, document the tool contract, and agree how tools change as your systems and the protocol evolve.

Before we begin

### Common questions about MCP server development and AI connectors

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**What is an MCP server, in practice?**
It is a small service that describes a set of tools and resources in a standard way, so any compatible AI application can use them without a bespoke integration. In practice it is ordinary backend engineering: authenticate, validate the input, call the underlying system, shape the response, log the call. The protocol is the straightforward part; the access model is the work.

**How is this different from your AI automation and RAG service?**
The AI automation, RAG and MCP development page covers the assistant itself: knowledge sources, retrieval, model behaviour and the user-facing workflow. This page covers the layer underneath it — the servers and connectors that give agents governed access to live systems. Many projects need both and they are often scoped together. If you are not sure which one you are asking for, describe the workflow and we will say.

**Can an agent be allowed to write data, not just read it?**
It can, with deliberate design. Write tools are kept separate from read tools, restricted to specific objects and operations, made idempotent where possible, and in most cases placed behind a human approval step that happens outside the model’s control. We would start read-only, prove tool selection is reliable, then add write capability one operation at a time.

**Which AI platforms can use what you build?**
Any MCP-compatible client, which now covers the major assistant and IDE products, plus platform-specific connectors and plugins where an organisation has standardised on one vendor. We test against the clients you actually use, because a tool description that works well in one client can be read differently in another.

**How do you stop prompt injection turning a tool into a problem?**
By not relying on the model to enforce anything. Permissions are checked server-side before a tool runs, tools expose only approved objects, generated SQL is validated against a whitelist, destructive operations are either not exposed or require human approval, and retrieved content is treated as data rather than as instructions. Logging every call means an unexpected request is visible afterwards, not merely prevented in theory.

**How much does custom MCP server development cost?**
We quote after a scoping call, and terms are agreed per engagement. The recommended starting point is small: one server, one system, one small group of users and the three or four tools that cover most of their requests. MV.tech is a remote-first team based in Ahmedabad, India, with a lean model that avoids large-consultancy overhead.

**How do you connect Claude or another AI assistant to our database safely?**
Instead of handing the assistant the keys, it calls an MCP server that runs under a scoped service identity against an approved set of tables, read-only by default and whitelisted rather than blocklisted. Where the agent generates SQL, the query is parsed and checked before it runs, with permitted objects only, row and cost limits and no writes, and results are validated before they are returned. Every call is logged with the caller, tool, time and outcome, and we test against real requests, including ones the server should refuse, before access is widened.

Related services

Scheduled workflows, webhooks, Apps Script and API integrations that replace manual hand-offs and make failures visible.

# Power BI Consultant: Semantic Models, DAX & Refresh | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/services/power-bi-consulting/
Description: Remote Power BI consulting: semantic models with an explicit grain, DAX, slow refresh fixes, SSAS migrations and KPI definitions reconciled to source.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

Service · Power BI consulting

## Power BI consulting: semantic models, DAX and refreshes that finish on time.

A Power BI report is only as good as the model underneath it. MV.tech provides remote Power BI consultants and developers who build semantic and dimensional models with an explicit grain, write and review DAX, fix slow refreshes, migrate SSAS and Azure Analysis Services models and reconcile every figure on a report back to its source. We review the model you already have before proposing that anything is rebuilt.

- Remote from Ahmedabad, India
- Overlap with your timezone
- Senior specialists, direct access
- Scope agreed in writing
The starting point

### When does a Power BI consultant make sense?

- A Power BI dashboard refresh is slow or times out, and the workaround so far has been to import less data.
- The model has grown report by report: no agreed grain, duplicated measures and DAX nobody wants to touch.
- Two reports answer the same question with different numbers and nobody can say which one is right.
- An SSAS or Azure Analysis Services model has to move to Power BI and nobody has documented what it contains.
- Analysts export to Excel because the published dataset cannot answer their follow-up question.
- A KPI exists in several reports with several definitions and no owner.
- You need a remote Power BI developer alongside your team for a defined phase rather than a permanent hire.
What we deliver

### What does a Power BI consultant deliver?

01

#### Semantic and dimensional models with an explicit grain

Star schemas with fact tables at a stated grain, conformed dimensions shared across subject areas, bridge tables where a relationship is genuinely many-to-many and a date table every measure filters through. The grain is written down before the first measure is, because most wrong totals in Power BI trace back to a fact table at the wrong grain rather than to the DAX on top of it.

02

#### DAX measures, calculation groups and Tabular Editor

Measures written once in the model and reused by every report, with calculation groups for time intelligence and currency rather than a copy per visual. Tabular Editor is used for scripted changes, measure organisation and best-practice rules, and DAX Studio for query timings, so a slow visual is traced to a specific measure rather than guessed at.

03

#### Source-to-target mappings

A written mapping per table: the source system and query, the warehouse or dataflow layer it passes through, the Power BI table and column, data types, transformation rules, keys and the check that proves it landed. It is what a reviewer reads to understand where a number came from, and it is what the reconciliation tests are generated from.

04

#### Refresh performance

Profile the model first: storage mode, column cardinality, calculated columns that belong upstream, unused columns and Power Query steps that stopped folding so whole tables are pulled before they are filtered. The usual fixes are incremental refresh with a proper partition policy, aggregation tables, pushing transformation back into the warehouse and removing what nothing reads, with refresh duration measured before and after on your own gateway or capacity.

05

#### SSAS and Azure Analysis Services migration

Document what the tabular model contains — tables, relationships, calculated columns, measures, roles and the reports depending on each — then move it into a Power BI semantic model through the XMLA endpoint, or rebuild it where the old model was itself the problem. Measures are compared old against new on identical filters before any report is repointed.

06

#### Governed KPI definitions

Each metric written down: the calculation, the filters, the grain, the owner and the reports it is allowed to appear on. Definitions live in the model's measure descriptions and in a catalogue your team can read without opening Power BI Desktop, so a KPI cannot quietly diverge between reports.

07

#### Self-service datasets

A shared dataset analysts can slice without writing joins: naming standards, hidden technical columns, a description on every field, row-level security where the data needs it and a clear line between governed measures and someone's own analysis. Thin reports connect live to it instead of each carrying its own copy of the data.

08

#### Reconciliation of report figures to source

Automated comparisons between what a report shows and what the source system holds: record counts, control totals, date coverage and the specific figures people act on, run on every refresh rather than once at sign-off. In a previous engagement at Volvo Cars via Toptal, MV.tech's founder designed fact and dimension models for Power BI with source-to-target mappings, built validation and reconciliation checks across source systems, Snowflake, Salesforce CRM Analytics and BI reports, and delivered a lead-to-sale matchback comparison across about 427K lead-month records for executive review.

Before we begin

### Questions about hiring a Power BI consultant.

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**Why is my Power BI dashboard refresh slow?**
Usually because the model imports more than it reads, or does work at refresh time that belongs in the warehouse. The common causes are calculated columns over large fact tables, high-cardinality columns such as timestamps or free text, Power Query steps that stop folding so a whole table is pulled before it is filtered, and a full refresh where an incremental policy would do. We profile the model with DAX Studio and the refresh history first, then change the few things that account for most of the time.

**What is a Power BI semantic model?**
It is the dataset layer between your warehouse and your reports: tables, relationships, measures, hierarchies and security roles. When it exists as one governed model, every report calculates revenue the same way and analysts can build their own views without writing joins. When each report carries its own copy of the data and its own measures, the numbers drift apart.

**Can you fix our existing Power BI model instead of rebuilding it?**
Usually, and that is the cheaper place to start. The review covers grain, relationships, calculated columns, duplicated measures, storage mode and refresh behaviour, and ends in a written list of what to fix in place and what genuinely needs remodelling. A rebuild is something we have to justify, not a starting assumption.

**Can you migrate our SSAS or Azure Analysis Services model to Power BI?**
Yes. The first step is documenting what the tabular model contains and which reports depend on each table and measure, because that decides whether it can move largely as-is through the XMLA endpoint or should be remodelled. Measures are compared old against new on identical filters before any report is repointed, and both models run in parallel until the figures are signed off.

**How much does Power BI consulting cost?**
We quote after a scoping call. The estimate depends on the number of reports and sources, the state of the existing model, whether an Analysis Services migration is involved and how much reconciliation the business needs to see. A review of one existing model is a bounded piece of work and is usually the cheapest way to find out what the rest would involve.

**Can a remote team in India work on our Power BI tenant?**
Yes. MV.tech works from India Standard Time and agrees an overlap window with your team before the engagement begins, with access through your own tenant, workspaces and gateway rather than through copies of your data. Changes go through deployment pipelines or version-controlled model files, so your team can see what changed and when.

**How do you prove the numbers on a report are right?**
By reconciling them to source and keeping the check running. Record counts, control totals and date coverage per table, plus the handful of figures people actually act on, are compared against the source system on every refresh. Differences are investigated and either fixed or written down as a deliberate change, which sometimes means the old report was the one that was wrong.

# Snowflake Consulting, Migration & Power BI Modelling | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/services/snowflake-consulting/
Description: Independent Snowflake consulting: migrate SQL Server, Oracle and spreadsheets into layered Snowflake, model for Power BI, reconcile sources and tune cost.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

Service · Snowflake consulting

## Snowflake consulting and migration from an independent engineering team.

Most Snowflake problems are design problems: one schema doing the job of four layers, warehouses sized by guesswork and Power BI figures that no longer match the source. MV.tech is not a Snowflake reseller or partner programme member; it works as an independent engineering team that migrates legacy reporting and SQL Server, Oracle and spreadsheet estates into Snowflake with raw, staging, curated and reporting layers, fact and dimension models for Power BI, and reconciliation at every stage. In a previous engagement at Volvo Cars via Toptal, MV.tech's founder migrated legacy and manual reporting into a Snowflake warehouse with those four layers, built fact and dimension models for Power BI with source-to-target mappings, and delivered a lead-to-sale matchback comparison between Volvo's attribution and an external vendor across about 427K lead-month records.

- Remote from Ahmedabad, India
- Overlap with your timezone
- Senior specialists, direct access
- Scope agreed in writing
The starting point

### When does a Snowflake consultant make sense?

- Reporting still runs on SQL Server, Oracle or a folder of spreadsheets, Snowflake has been chosen as the target, and nobody has mapped what depends on the old estate.
- Snowflake is already in place, but everything landed in one schema with no raw, staging, curated or reporting separation to build on.
- Power BI reads Snowflake through hand-written queries rather than fact and dimension tables, so every report calculates its own version of revenue.
- Monthly credit consumption keeps rising and nobody can say which warehouses, queries or refreshes are responsible.
- Figures in Snowflake, Salesforce CRM Analytics and the finance system disagree, and reconciling them is a manual job each month.
- Ingestion through Azure Data Factory or Python jobs works most days, with no validation that would catch the days it does not.
- A previous migration attempt stalled because the new numbers did not match the old ones and no one could explain why.
What we deliver

### What does Snowflake consulting from MV.tech include?

01

#### Migration from SQL Server, Oracle and spreadsheets

Catalogue the source estate from the information schema, DDL, query logs and job schedules, then write a source-to-target mapping per object: target table and layer, data types, transformation rules, keys, grain and historical scope. Spreadsheet reporting is handled the same way, with the rules that live in formulas written down before they are modelled. Each load is reconciled against the legacy figures so cutover happens on evidence rather than on a date.

02

#### Raw, staging, curated and reporting layers

Design Snowflake as four separated layers: raw as it arrived, staging typed and conformed, curated facts and dimensions, and reporting views shaped for the tools that read them. Each layer has an owner, a refresh dependency and a check that proves it loaded, which is what keeps the warehouse maintainable after the project ends.

03

#### Fact and dimension models for Power BI

Build fact and dimension tables at an agreed grain, with conformed dimensions, bridge tables for many-to-many relationships and source-load tracking, then the curated views Power BI imports or queries directly. Existing Power BI and DAX models are profiled first, so a rebuild is a justified decision rather than a default.

04

#### Views and curated datasets

Publish curated datasets analysts can query without writing joins: consistent naming, a description on every column, technical fields hidden and governed measures kept apart from someone's own analysis. Secure views and role-based grants control who sees what without copying the data.

05

#### Validation and reconciliation across sources

Automated comparison at each stage: record counts, date coverage, nulls, duplicates, control totals and metric-level comparison of the figures people report, across the source systems, Snowflake and the BI layer. Differences are explained rather than rounded away, and each one ends as a fix or a documented, deliberate change.

06

#### Cost and performance tuning

Reduce what each query reads and what each warehouse costs: clustering keys chosen against real query patterns, warehouse sizes and auto-suspend settings taken from the query history rather than guesswork, incremental loads in place of full refreshes, and materialised results where a report reads the same aggregate every hour. The before-and-after is measured on your own queries and credit consumption.

07

#### Salesforce CRM Analytics and Azure Data Factory ingestion

Where reporting already lives in Salesforce CRM Analytics, handle the datasets, recipes, dataflows and field mapping so Snowflake and CRM Analytics agree on the same figures. Where sources sit in Azure, build Azure Data Factory pipelines through Blob Storage into Snowflake with incremental loads, retries and logging, and Python and SQL ingestion elsewhere.

08

#### Handover and operating documentation

Mappings, ER diagrams, validation results, refresh schedules, the role and grant model, cost monitoring and runbooks, written for the people who will run Snowflake after the engagement. Handover is part of the scope, not an extra.

- SQL

A useful first project

### What is a sensible first Snowflake project?

One reporting domain, taken the whole way. Pick finance, sales or operations and cover discovery of its sources, source-to-target mapping, the four Snowflake layers, a fact and dimension model, reconciliation against the figures people trust today and one Power BI report repointed at the result. It is small enough to correct cheaply and complete enough to prove the layer design, the validation approach and the cost profile on your data. The remaining domains are then estimated from what the first one showed rather than from a template, and we quote after a scoping call.

Working together

### A practical path from scope to delivery.

- 01 — Discover and map — Profile the source estate, its dependencies and any existing Snowflake usage, agree the layer design and write the source-to-target mapping and migration sequence.
- 02 — Build and reconcile — Load and model one domain at a time, comparing each layer with the source on counts, coverage, totals and reported metrics before the next domain begins.
- 03 — Tune, cut over and hand over — Set clustering, warehouse sizing and refresh schedules from real query history, repoint Power BI on evidence, and hand over mappings, grants and runbooks.

Before we begin

### Questions about Snowflake consulting.

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**Is MV.tech a Snowflake consulting partner?**
No. MV.tech is not a Snowflake reseller or a member of the Snowflake partner programme; it works as an independent engineering team that designs, migrates and tunes Snowflake warehouses on your own Snowflake account. You buy Snowflake from Snowflake and engineering from us, so there is no resale margin in the advice. The founder holds the Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer certification; MV.tech makes no Snowflake certification or partner claims.

**How much does Snowflake consulting cost?**
For Snowflake work, we quote after a scoping call. The estimate depends on the number of source systems, the volume of historical data, how much logic is hidden in views, stored procedures and spreadsheets, the Power BI models to be repointed and the support expected afterwards. A first domain is scoped as a bounded piece of work so the figure for the rest of the estate rests on your data rather than on a template.

**How do you migrate SQL Server or Oracle to Snowflake without breaking reports?**
Dependency analysis first, reconciliation throughout. Before anything moves we trace which reports, extracts and semantic models read each object and flag the platform-specific SQL, cross-database joins and hardcoded rules that will not survive the move. Layers are then built and compared with the legacy numbers stage by stage, and dashboards are repointed visual by visual, usually while both platforms run in parallel.

**Should Power BI connect to Snowflake with Import or DirectQuery?**
Import for most governed reporting, DirectQuery where data must be current to the minute or is too large to hold in memory, and a composite model when one report needs both. The more important decision is upstream: Power BI should read fact and dimension tables and curated views from the reporting layer, not raw tables, so the model stays small and the business logic lives in one place. We profile the existing model before recommending a change.

**Why is our Snowflake bill rising, and can you reduce it?**
Usually because warehouses stay awake for queries that scan more than they should. The common causes are missing clustering on large tables, full refreshes where incremental loads would do, oversized warehouses with long auto-suspend settings and reports that repeat the same aggregate many times an hour. We measure from the query history, change the few things that account for most of the spend and show the before-and-after on your own credit consumption.

**Can a remote team in India run our Snowflake migration?**
Yes. MV.tech works from Ahmedabad, India, and agrees a collaboration window in your timezone before work begins: US Eastern mornings, UK and European business hours, Gulf hours or Asia-Pacific afternoons. Snowflake work suits remote delivery because access is role-based and every change can be reviewed as SQL in a pull request. Reconciliation results, decisions and handover notes are written down where your team can read them the next morning.

**Can you reconcile Snowflake with Salesforce CRM Analytics and our finance system?**
Yes, and it is often the part that earns trust in the warehouse. We compare the same metric across the source systems, Snowflake and the CRM Analytics or BI layer at an agreed grain, then investigate every difference until it is fixed or documented as a deliberate change. That investigation sometimes shows that the legacy figure was the wrong one.

# Workflow Automation Consulting & API Integration | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/services/workflow-automation/
Description: Workflow automation consulting from a remote team in India working in your timezone: API integrations, scheduled jobs, reconciliation checks and monitoring.
Last modified: 2026-10-12

Service · Remote-first senior specialists

## Workflow automation and API integration consulting

Connect the steps between your business systems. MV.tech builds API integrations, scheduled workflows, spreadsheet and add-on automation, and the operational plumbing around them — reducing repeated manual work and making failures visible.

- Remote from Ahmedabad, India
- Overlap with your timezone
- Senior specialists, direct access
- Scope agreed in writing
The starting point

### When does workflow automation make sense?

- People repeatedly move the same records between business tools and spreadsheets.
- Scheduled reports rely on manual downloads, cleanup and distribution.
- Finance or operations reconcile two systems by hand every month and the differences are never documented.
- A spreadsheet has quietly become a business system, with formulas and scripts nobody owns.
- An integration works on the happy path but produces duplicate actions after a retry.
- A script runs in the background without clear ownership, status checks or recovery steps.
What we deliver

### What does a workflow automation engagement deliver?

01

#### API and webhook integrations

Connect approved business systems using their supported interfaces: REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth flows and blockchain RPCs. Handle pagination, rate limits, authentication and changes in source records.

02

#### Scheduled business workflows

Automate recurring data pulls, report preparation, exports and status checks in Python and SQL. Define the schedule, inputs and expected output for each step, and run them somewhere accountable — Cloud Run, a container or scheduled CI, rather than a laptop.

03

#### Spreadsheet and add-on automation

Where the process genuinely lives in Google Sheets or Excel, automate it there: Google Apps Script jobs, Sheets add-ons, controlled exports and usage logging. Keep the calculation in a governed source and let the spreadsheet be the interface.

04

#### Reconciliation and exception handling

Add checks before data is written or a downstream action is triggered: matching, tolerance rules, duplicate prevention and retries. Where a figure must be adjusted by hand, an override layer can record the change without altering the immutable source record, which leaves an audit trail instead of an argument.

05

#### Web and document data extraction

Collect data that has no API. Maintainable Python scraping of dynamic pages and authenticated portals, respecting source terms and rate limits, plus LLM-assisted extraction from documents where the layout keeps changing.

06

#### Monitoring, deployment and ownership

Provide logs, useful alerts and operating documentation, with deployment through Docker and GitHub Actions so a change is reviewable. Make it clear who maintains a workflow and how to recover or rerun it when a dependency fails.

- Python
- REST APIs
- Webhooks
- OAuth
- SQL
- Google Apps Script
- Google Sheets add-ons
- Cloud Run
- Docker
- GitHub Actions
- Scheduled jobs
- Cloud Logging
- Reporting workflows
A useful first project

### What is a good first workflow automation project?

Pick a recurring handoff with a clear input and output, such as preparing a weekly report from several systems or reconciling two ledgers. Document what people check today, including exceptions and the adjustments they make by hand. The project can then automate the repeatable steps while preserving review where judgment is required. Assess the result using completion time, exception frequency, how much manual reconciliation is left and the effort needed to recover a failed run.

Working together

### A practical path from scope to delivery.

- 01 — Observe the current workflow — Map triggers, source tools, manual checks, exceptions and who receives the result.
- 02 — Connect and validate — Implement the integrations and test retries, missing data and downstream failures as well as a successful run.
- 03 — Schedule and hand over — Agree operating hours, alert recipients, access ownership and a recovery procedure.

Before we begin

### Common questions about workflow automation consulting

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**Can you automate a workflow across several tools?**
Yes, when the tools provide suitable authorised access. We review available APIs, webhooks, exports and authentication before estimating the integration. Source limits and downstream permissions shape what can be automated reliably.

**Does every automation need AI?**
No. A scheduled job or API integration may be enough for a predictable process. AI is useful when a step requires language or document interpretation, and that step still needs suitable evaluation and review.

**How do you avoid duplicate records or repeated actions?**
The workflow can include stable record identifiers, state tracking, reconciliation and checks before writing. The exact design depends on whether the connected systems support safe retries and how costly a repeated action would be.

**Can you maintain automations built by another developer?**
Yes. An initial review can establish the code, schedules, dependencies, access requirements and failure history. We can then scope a repair, documentation or ongoing support engagement.

**How much does workflow automation consulting cost?**
Pricing is agreed per engagement and we quote after a scoping call. A useful first project is one recurring handoff with a clear input and output, such as preparing a weekly report from several systems or reconciling two ledgers. The estimate depends on the APIs, webhooks, exports and authentication the connected tools provide, since source limits and downstream permissions shape what can be automated reliably.

**How do you reconcile finance data across two systems?**
We start by documenting what people check today, including the exceptions and the adjustments they make by hand. The workflow then applies matching, tolerance rules, duplicate prevention and retries before any data is written or a downstream action is triggered. Where a figure must still be adjusted manually, an override layer can record the change without altering the immutable source record, which leaves an audit trail instead of an argument.

# Solution Patterns: Data Platforms, Portals & AI Assistants | MV.tech

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/solutions/
Description: Systems MV.tech builds most often: governed data layers, warehouse migrations, reconciliation layers, portals and internal apps, and AI knowledge assistants.
Last modified: 2026-10-07

Solution patterns

## Practical systems for real operating teams.

Most of the work we are asked for falls into a few recognisable shapes. These patterns show what a first release usually contains and where it tends to grow next. Each one is shaped around your workflows, data sources and stage of growth.

Data platform

### Business data operating layer

Connect APIs, databases, spreadsheets and external feeds into a governed reporting layer your team can trust. Definitions live in one place, refreshes are monitored, and every number can be traced to its source.

- ETL/ELT pipelines and warehouse models in BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift or PostgreSQL
- Data quality checks, alerts and recovery paths
- Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio or Streamlit views, with exports that match the screen
Web & app

### Customer portal or internal app

Ship a clean interface for customers, operators or administrators with forms, user flows, integrations and analytics. Built around one complete user journey first, then extended as the process matures.

- Responsive UI and API-backed workflows
- Role-based access, approvals and audit trails
- Maintainable code and documented handover
AI & automation

### Knowledge assistant for teams

Give a team a controlled assistant over documents, structured data and workflow APIs, with answers grounded in source context and actions limited to what has been approved.

- RAG over documents, tickets and business data
- MCP servers and custom AI connectors into approved tools, with human approval
- Access-aware, evaluated and auditable implementation
Migration

### Legacy reporting moved to a cloud warehouse

Move reporting off legacy databases, extracts and spreadsheets into Snowflake or BigQuery without losing the numbers people already rely on. Discovery first, then layers, then a cutover justified by evidence rather than a date.

- Database discovery, source-to-target mapping and dependency analysis
- Raw, staging, curated and reporting layers with fact and dimension models
- Stage-by-stage reconciliation against the reports in use today
Data quality

### Reconciliation and validation layer

When two systems disagree every month, the fix is a layer that compares them on a schedule, explains the difference and records any adjustment. The source data stays immutable; the corrections sit above it with an audit trail.

- Record counts, date coverage, nulls, duplicates, totals and metric comparisons
- Matching and tolerance rules, outlier detection and alerting
- Manual-override and whitelist layers that leave the base dataset untouched
On-chain data

### Cross-chain transaction ledger

For teams whose data lives on several networks, a warehouse-backed ledger that consolidates activity into consistent, valued and categorised records that finance and operations can query like any other dataset.

- Transactions, logs and events decoded with contract ABIs and Web3.py
- FX reference data, token-level valuation and fee proration
- Transaction categorisation, staking-reward reconciliation and KPI reporting
Two more common shapes

### Operational automation and an embedded specialist.

### Repeated hand-off, automated

A weekly report assembled from four systems, invoices pushed from one tool to another, records reconciled by hand. We automate the repeatable steps, keep review where judgment is needed, and make failures visible with logs and alerts.

### Senior specialist inside your team

When the shape of the work is still emerging, an embedded data, software or AI consultant working in your tools and your hours is often the fastest route. Capacity, responsibilities and overlap are agreed before the start.

How a pattern becomes a project

### Start small, prove it, then extend.

- 01 — Pick one workflow — One report, one journey, one hand-off, one knowledge set. Enough to matter, small enough to judge in weeks.
- 02 — Agree acceptance — What "working" means: which records, how fresh, who can see what, what happens on failure.
- 03 — Deliver and decide — A working release with documentation and monitoring, then a conversation about the next useful increment.
Which pattern fits?

### Describe your workflow and we will map it to a first release.

Bring the goal, the systems involved and your preferred working hours. Thirty minutes is enough to propose a sensible first milestone.
